title: Suggest a lesson question the text answers
statement: For a text without a lesson question, draft several and keep one only on a judge's positive evidence that the text answers it.
example: In the 12 October run a poem and a speech each got a usable open question this way, and all 32 blocks were made from those two questions.
detail: For a text that comes without a question, the lesson engine asks a writer for three open questions answerable from the text alone, keeps those code finds well formed, and keeps the first one a judge finds answerable from the passage and worth a lesson of about an hour, on positive evidence. The result is cached under a hash of the text, so the same text is always given the same question. In the 12 October run both new texts got a usable open question this way, and every block on each was made from it.
against: The judge is asked two things at once, whether the question can be answered from the passage alone and whether it is worth a lesson of about an hour. The poem's suggested question was also narrower than the sample question it came with: 5 of its 14 lines were ranked for it, against 13 lines judged relevant to the sample question in the 9 October proof. With no judge present, the lesson engine keeps and caches the first well-formed draft unchecked (`g9/transformer/src/question.js`, lines 31-37).

evidence.quote: positive evidence. Cached by text, so the same text is given the same question.
